content.overview: Specialists protect product and evidence by controlling status and escalating. They should not convert incomplete evidence into an unauthorized disposition decision.

vocabulary.definition: Controlled status preventing specified movement or use while evaluation remains open.
Authorized decision governing the allowed next state of material.
Defined condition requiring transfer to a role with additional authority or expertise.

sections.title: Status must be visible and recorded
sections.body: Physical segregation, system status and lot identity should agree so material cannot move inadvertently.

sections.title: Escalation carries the evidence packet
sections.body: The next role needs event facts, scope, samples, results, open questions and interim controls rather than a conclusion without support.

sections.title: Disposition authority remains explicit
sections.body: Release, rework, rejection and destruction require the applicable authorized role and controlled record; specialists may recommend without self-authorizing.

workedExamples: A specialist documents suspected mold, places connected lots on controlled hold and transfers the evidence for qualified disposition.
commonMistakes: Releasing unaffected-looking units without scope review.
Using an undocumented verbal instruction to change status.
content.practicalApplication: Create a hold-and-escalation record with lot scope, reason, controls, evidence, decision owner and status-change history.
content.summary: Hold and escalation preserve safety and evidence while disposition remains with the authorized decision process.
